abstract: Splicing of the primary transcript is a major step to produce the mature mRNA. While the biochemistry of the splicing mechanism has been elucidated in detail, the dynamics and structural arrangements inside the nucleus are not clear. Biochemical and genomic studies of splicing and transcription most often lose the information about individual states and localization from the sub-nuclear to the tissue level by averaging over populations and homogenization of cells and tissues. Imaging approaches, which would overcome these problems, have been hampered by the short length of most genes, preventing discrimination between different regions like introns and exons along the transcript due to limited resolution. To overcome these limitations, we apply high-resolution microscopy with Airyscan joint-deconvolution to the megabase transcription units of Drosophila Y-loops. Along these extended chromatin fibers, we can directly observe the linear arrangement and local splicing events of introns and exons as well as the corresponding 3D chromatin structure. We compare these events between primary spermatocytes at different stages of their development within whole-mount testes. We show that co-transcriptional splicing of the Y-loop A transcript exhibits delayed splicing. The extent of this delay differs between transcription clusters along the same chromatin fiber within a nucleus and the average splicing delay increases with spermatocyte maturation. This shows that co-ordination of splicing and transcription is regulated locally at the site of transcription and by developmental state. We find that the concentration of the transcriptional activator Eaf is inversely correlated with spermatocyte maturation thus suggesting that the decreased frequency of transcription pause/pause release may be responsible for the splicing delay. Consistently, we find hubs containing the spliceosome with elongating and paused RNA-polymerase together with Eaf in chromatin bends. From their different arrangements we derive a model for splicing hub biogenesis.
